newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends down despite central bank support.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends down despite central bank support.

text.p: The won finished sharply lower versus the dollar on Tuesday despite the central bank's dollar selling intervention, traders said.
But the bank denied the move as it regularly does.
The won closed at 858.30 after opening at 856.40. The won hit a low of 858.60 in the afternoon, the lowest since a market average system was introduced in March 1990.
Dealers said banks were actively collecting dollars to help cover their large import settlements. A Stronger dollar against the Japanese yen in world markets also fuelled dollar buying.
They said the local unit was expected to fall further as exports are likely to flag following labour unrest and Hanbo Steel's loan default.
"The dollar is set to rise further in the near future," said one local trader.
The base mid-rate is seen at 857.50 for Wednesday, compared with 855.00 for Tuesday.
